visual_action: The video is a slideshow of still images set to music. It begins with a screenshot of a tweet from 'FactPost' showing Donald Trump and an ornate ballroom. It then cuts to three images of a blonde woman at a White House press podium, with different yellow text overlaid on each image. In the final of these three images, she holds up a rendering of a building. The video then shows a wide shot of a large, empty, opulent ballroom, and concludes with a screenshot of a CNBC news headline.

cast.name: Donald Trump
cast.evidence: The on-screen text refers to "The Trump administration" and "Trump's 'big beautiful bill'." A photo of him is also shown.

cast.name: unnamed White House official
cast.evidence: A woman is shown in three separate photos standing at the White House press briefing podium, presented as an official making an announcement.

cast.name: FactPost
cast.evidence: A screenshot of a tweet from the account 'FactPost @factpostnews' is shown at the beginning of the video.

cast.name: CNBC
cast.evidence: A screenshot of a news headline from CNBC is shown at the end of the video.

on_screen_text.text: The Trump administration has announced they will be building a $200 million ballroom at the White House.
This comes weeks after passing a law that will kick 17 million Americans off their health care.
The construction of the new White House ballroom will soon begin.
The White House is unable to hold major functions without having to install an unsightly tent.
The $200M ballroom will be an exquisite addition of 90,000 square feet.
Medicaid cuts in Trump's 'big beautiful bill' will leave millions uninsured, threaten rural hospitals

spoken_summary: A female voice says, "Let them eat cake." This is immediately followed by an energetic indie rock song with female vocals that plays for the remainder of the video.
audio_music: The video opens with the spoken phrase "Let them eat cake," which then transitions into an upbeat, fast-paced indie rock song ('Deceptacon' by Le Tigre) that continues until the end. The music creates a frantic and energetic mood, juxtaposing with the serious political topics presented.
editing_pacing: The video is a fast-paced slideshow, cutting between a series of static images and screenshots in time with the music.
manipulation_or_satire: The video presents satirical content as factual. The 'announcement' about the ballroom is conveyed through still images of an actress from the comedy show 'The Opposition w/ Jordan Klepper,' with fabricated quotes superimposed as text. The initial tweet is from 'FactPost,' a known satirical account. This content is presented as a real news report to mislead the viewer.
central_claim: The Trump administration is callously spending $200 million on a lavish ballroom while simultaneously cutting healthcare for 17 million Americans.
intended_effect: To generate anger and outrage at the Trump administration for its perceived elitism and misplaced priorities.
